covers.desc: Be able to interpret the correlation coefficient r, including its range, direction, and strength using standard cutoff conventions.
Be able to identify the dependent and independent variables in a regression setting and distinguish the population regression equation from the estimated regression line, including residuals.
Be able to compute the slope and y-intercept of the least-squares regression line from summary statistics and interpret both in context.
Be able to compute the coefficient of determination R-squared and interpret it as the percentage of variation in the response variable explained by the model.
Be able to compute correlation and least-squares regression output (slope, intercept, r, R-squared) using Excel and Python.
